Today in AI NOW & BEYOND 🔥 Deploy Self-Hosted AI Agents Deploy Self-Hosted AI Agents with One-Click Setup AI Highlights of the Week Too Important to Miss Deploy Self-Hosted AI Agents with One-Click Setup Sponsored AI agents are becoming capable of much more than answering questions. They can handle recurring research, run scheduled tasks, remember context across sessions, and develop new skills over time. OpenClaw and Hermes Agent are built to bring these capabilities to self-hosted environments. With one-click Marketplace apps on Vultr, you can deploy them on cloud infrastructure and start building your own AI-powered workflows. Launch OpenClaw & Hermes Agent Instantly Claude Helped Researchers Break Into OpenAI Three researchers reached employee accounts and internal repositories in less than 72 hours Hacktron researchers combined flaws in OpenAI’s community forum and login system to take over employee accounts. With Claude’s help, they demonstrated access to internal repositories without reading the code, then reported their findings. Key Points: New Model, Different Result: Opus 4.8 struggled to build a working exploit, but Opus 5 succeeded within hours of its release. Codex Proved the Breach: The team used an employee’s Codex account to submit a harmless proposed change to OpenAI’s private code repository. A Surprisingly Small Bill: Their wider investigation across several companies cost under $3,000 in AI tokens, with three researchers doing the work. Fixed and Rewarded: OpenAI confirmed its fix roughly 14 hours after the report and paid $6,500 for the OpenAI vulnerability, not the forum attack. Why It Matters: AI is making sophisticated hacking cheaper, though skilled researchers still guided this work. The warning for businesses is how far one compromised account can reach when AI assistants connect it to code, email and other company tools. It also adds Claude Docs and Claude Slides, so users can create, edit, present, and export documents or presentations directly from the same conversation. 80092.subject: 🔷 The Daily: Bitcoin ETFs end 9-day inflow streak
80092.body:
Bitcoin ETFs snap 9-day, $3.1 billion inflow streak | NEAR Intents partially resumes services after $3.8 million exploit | Lloyds, Visa settle $750,000 using USDC in live cross-border pilot | Hyperliquid Policy Center, Circle press EU on perps and stablecoin reserves in MiCA review | Clarity Act's failure gave crypto 'faster' regulatory wins, Bitwise CIO says

The Daily ( https://www.theblock.co/?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

Written by Yogita Khatri | Edited by Kyle Baird

Presented By:

( https://thezcashetf.com/?utm_campaign=website-traffic-zcsh-newsletters--2026-08-25&utm_medium=paid-other&utm_source=the-block&utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

Happy Thursday! *Bitcoin* is up today, trading around *$84,700* , while *U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs* ended a nine-day, *$3 billion* inflow streak as *$149 million* exited the funds on Wednesday.

Also in today's newsletter, *NEAR Intents* suffered a *$3.8 million* *exploit* , *Lloyds* and *Visa* settled *$750,000* using *USDC* in a live cross-border pilot, *Hyperliquid Policy Center* and *Circle* are pushing for changes to EU crypto rules, and more.

Meanwhile, *Robinhood Wallet* integrates ( https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-10-01-robinhood-wallet-integrates-arcus-rfq-system-for-stock-token-swaps-417394?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) *Arcus'* RFQ system for stock token swaps, and an *Ethereum* staking reward burn proposal is pulled ( https://www.theblock.co/news/ecosystems/2026-10-01-ethereum-staking-reward-burn-proposal-eip-8363-pulled-hegota-upgrade-417419?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) from the *Hegota* upgrade.

P.S. Don't forget to check out The Latent ( https://thelatent.co/?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) , our sister website covering AI. Get The Latent Daily here ( https://thelatent.co/newsletter?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) and all other The Block newsletters here ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ).

*THE BIG ONE*

*📉 Bitcoin ETFs snap 9-day, $3.1 billion inflow streak*

( https://www.theblock.co/news/markets/2026-10-01-bitcoin-etfs-9-day-3-billion-inflow-streak-comes-to-an-end-as-149-million-exits-the-funds-417384?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

*U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs* recorded *$148.7 million in combined net outflows* on Wednesday, ending a nine-day streak that brought in *$3.1 billion*.

* *BlackRock's IBIT* also ended its own nine-day inflow run, which had brought in $1.6 billion, with *$9.5 million in net outflows* on Wednesday.
* *Fidelity's FBTC* led the day's outflows with *$125.6 million* , followed by *Bitwise's BITB* with $13.6 million. All remaining funds registered zero flows.

 When I was a student I sold Christmas cards to raise money for UNICEF. To potential donors sipping ale in English pubs, I’d stress that for less than the price of a pint they could pay for a vaccine shot that might save the life of a child in Africa. Many reached for their wallets, but I remember one who said, in a rather peeved voice: “Why don’t you raise money for British children?”
